idea: Confirm the current codex non-blocking background-completion wake path and decide whether overflowed background output should spill to a file for Claude Code + Copilot parity. Current behavior is inline-only: spawn_exit_watcher builds BackgroundCompletionEvent.output from build_background_completion_output(...) in core/src/unified_exec/async_watcher.rs, caps wake output at 16 KiB, and emits only a head/tail preview with an omission marker. The old await_background_completion retrieval tool was removed in 7133aca92, so oversized output currently has no recovery path.

missingLenses.reason: malformed (timed out without writing staged output)

candidateDirections.name: Experimental tee-to-session artifact + truncated wake reference
candidateDirections.summary: Recommended. Keep the current inline wake preview, but gate a default-off fork feature that tees full background output during streaming into a session-scoped artifact and appends a recovery reference when the wake payload truncates. Use a session-owned path under ~/.codex/sessions/<conversation>/... rather than OS temp, and keep the implementation to a small unified-exec seam plus helper logic so the fork can preserve parity without pretending exit-time spill can recover bytes already dropped by HeadTailBuffer.

candidateDirections.name: Typed artifact handle or retrieval seam instead of a raw file path
candidateDirections.summary: If privacy, batching, or prompt-coupling concerns dominate, prefer a typed artifact handle or retrieval seam over embedding a literal filesystem path in <task_notification>. This costs more design surface up front, but it survives notification coalescing better and avoids binding model behavior to a local path string.

candidateDirections.name: Keep current inline truncation until real workflows prove the gap hurts
candidateDirections.summary: Do nothing beyond the current 16 KiB head/tail wake payload until real background completions show that the omitted middle is frequently actionable. Lowest-change option, but it preserves the parity gap with Claude/Copilot and leaves the agent unable to recover long background output without rerunning commands.

questionsForSynthesis: Is the real requirement to recover outputs larger than 16 KiB, or larger than the 1 MiB HeadTailBuffer retention cap? Only the latter forces tee-before-omission rather than spill-on-exit.
Should the wake payload expose a raw filesystem path, or should the fork add a typed artifact reference or retrieval seam for cleaner privacy and future compatibility?
How should multi-completion batching preserve spill references, given that the current coalescer in core/src/tasks/mod.rs only retains task_id and exit_code from queued background notifications?
Should spilled artifacts follow the hook spiller's OS-temp pattern, or the session-owned ~/.codex/sessions/<id>/... pattern already used by other codex sidecars and artifacts?
What cleanup and retention policy is acceptable for potentially large, sensitive background-output artifacts?
